baslik: An Empty Fuel Tank Destroyed TWA Flight 800
sonuc: exploded shortly after take-off from New York
tetik: fuel vapour in a nearly empty centre tank
mekanizma: ignition of flammable fuel-air vapour in the centre wing tank, most likely from a wiring fault
ders: the FAA required systems that reduce fuel tank flammability, such as nitrogen inerting
zincir: HOT DAY, AIR-CON PACKS HEAT IT
yanilgi: An empty fuel tank is not safe. A nearly empty tank full of warm vapour can be more explosive than a full one.
tartisma: Nitrogen inerting took years to be required. How fast should a fix follow a finding?
basliklar: Why TWA Flight 800 Exploded
The Danger of an Empty Fuel Tank
sahneler: Minutes after take-off, a jumbo jet exploded off Long Island.
It broke apart and fell into the ocean, killing everyone aboard.
Investigators traced the blast to the centre fuel tank.
That tank was nearly empty.
Heat from the air-conditioning units warmed the vapour inside.
Warm fuel vapour is far easier to ignite than liquid fuel.
A spark, most likely from wiring, set it off.
New rules now require airliners to make those tanks far less flammable.

baslik: The Mislabelled Boxes That Burned ValuJet 592
sonuc: crashed into the Everglades after a cargo fire
tetik: expired oxygen generators loaded as cargo without safety caps
mekanizma: chemical oxygen generators activating in a cargo hold with no fire detection or suppression
ders: cargo holds got smoke detectors and fire suppression, and oxygen generators were banned as cargo
yanilgi: The generators were not empty canisters. They were expired but still able to produce oxygen and intense heat.
tartisma: Several companies handled the boxes and nobody caught the error. Who owns a hazard that passes through many hands?
basliklar: Why ValuJet Flight 592 Crashed
The Cargo That Fed Its Own Fire
sahneler: A passenger jet dove into the Florida Everglades.
A cargo fire burned into the cabin, and everyone aboard died.
The fuel for that fire was in boxes of oxygen generators.
They had been labelled as empty.
In fact they were expired but still live, with no safety caps.
When one activated, it made heat and pure oxygen.
The hold had no smoke detector and no way to fight fire.
Cargo holds now carry detectors and fire suppression.

baslik: Too Little Grease Brought Down Alaska 261
tetik: a jackscrew nut worn out by too little lubrication
mekanizma: stripped acme nut threads on the horizontal stabilizer trim jackscrew
ders: lubrication and end-play inspection intervals were tightened
yanilgi: The jackscrew didn't break suddenly. Its nut wore down over years because maintenance intervals had been stretched.
tartisma: Each extension of the maintenance interval looked small. How do small savings add up to a failure?
basliklar: Why Alaska Airlines Flight 261 Crashed
The Worn Thread That Controlled a Jet
sahneler: An airliner suddenly pitched down and dove into the Pacific.
The pilots fought it for minutes, but all eighty eight aboard died.
The tail's trim was driven by a single jackscrew.
Its nut needed regular grease.
Maintenance intervals had been stretched again and again.
The threads wore away until the nut could no longer hold.
The tail slipped, and the jet became uncontrollable.
Lubrication and wear checks were tightened across the fleet.

baslik: The Forklift Shortcut That Tore an Engine Off a DC-10
sonuc: crashed after an engine tore off at take-off
tetik: a maintenance shortcut that cracked the engine pylon
mekanizma: pylon bulkhead cracked by removing engine and pylon together with a forklift
ders: the shortcut was banned and slat systems were given locking protection
yanilgi: Losing one engine should not bring down a DC-10. The torn pylon also cut lines that held the wing's slats out.
tartisma: The shortcut saved hundreds of work hours. How should an airline approve a new maintenance procedure?
basliklar: Why American Airlines Flight 191 Crashed
The Maintenance Shortcut That Cracked a Pylon
sahneler: As a DC-10 lifted off from Chicago, its left engine tore away.
The jet rolled over and crashed, killing everyone aboard and two on the ground.
The damage had been done weeks earlier, during maintenance.
To save time, workers removed engine and pylon together with a forklift.
That cracked the pylon's mounting.
At take-off, it broke and cut hydraulic lines.
The slats on one wing retracted, and that wing stalled.
The shortcut was banned, and slats got protection against retracting.

baslik: The Rudder Inputs That Snapped Off a Tail
sonuc: lost its tail fin shortly after take-off
tetik: repeated full rudder inputs in wake turbulence
mekanizma: aerodynamic loads from alternating rudder inputs exceeding the vertical stabilizer's strength
ders: airline pilot training changed to warn against aggressive rudder reversals
yanilgi: The composite tail wasn't defective. It broke under loads beyond what it was designed to carry.
tartisma: The pilot's training had encouraged rudder use in upsets. When training is wrong, who is at fault?
basliklar: Why American Airlines Flight 587 Lost Its Tail
The Rudder Pedal That Broke an Airliner
soru: Was it the pilot or the training?
sahneler: Moments after take-off from New York, an Airbus lost its tail fin.
It crashed in Queens, killing everyone aboard and five on the ground.
It had flown into another jet's wake turbulence.
The first officer pushed the rudder hard, left then right.
Each swing built up huge sideways loads on the tail.
That exceeded the fin's design strength.
The fin snapped off, and the jet went out of control.
Pilot training changed to warn against aggressive rudder reversals.

baslik: Ice on the Sensors Made the Engines Lie
sonuc: crashed into a bridge and the frozen Potomac River
tetik: iced engine sensors showing more thrust than the engines made
mekanizma: engine anti-ice left off, so iced pressure probes gave false thrust readings, plus ice on the wings
ders: de-icing and winter take-off procedures were overhauled
yanilgi: The engines weren't failing. They were working normally, but the gauges said they were producing more power than they were.
tartisma: The first officer said something seemed wrong but the take-off continued. How should doubt be voiced in a cockpit?
basliklar: Why Air Florida Flight 90 Crashed
The Gauges That Lied in a Snowstorm
sahneler: In a snowstorm, a jet struck a bridge and plunged into the frozen Potomac.
Cars on the bridge were crushed, and most people aboard were killed.
The crew thought they had full take-off power.
They didn't.
Engine anti-ice was off, and ice had blocked the pressure probes.
The gauges read high while the engines made less thrust.
With snow on the wings too, the jet couldn't climb.
Winter de-icing and take-off procedures were overhauled.

baslik: A Cargo Door Opened Over the Pacific
sonuc: had its cargo door burst open in flight
tetik: an electrical fault unlatching a door whose locks were too weak
mekanizma: cargo door latches driven open by a faulty switch or wiring, with locking sectors unable to stop them
ders: 747 cargo door locks were strengthened across the fleet
yanilgi: The door wasn't left open by the crew. The latches were driven open electrically, and the locks were too weak to stop them.
tartisma: Weaknesses in the locks had been reported before. How serious must a report be to force a fleet-wide fix?
basliklar: Why United Airlines Flight 811's Door Blew Open
The Locks That Couldn't Hold the Door
sahneler: Over the Pacific, a 747's cargo door blew open.
A section of the cabin ripped away, and nine passengers were killed.
The pilots turned back and landed in Honolulu.
The door's latches had been driven open electrically.
A faulty switch or wiring set them moving.
The locks meant to stop that were too weak.
The door's recovery from the ocean proved it.
Locks on 747 cargo doors were then strengthened.

baslik: A Fan Blade Broke and a Window Blew Out
sonuc: had an engine fail and a window break in flight
tetik: a fatigue crack in one fan blade
mekanizma: fan blade fatigue fracture causing an uncontained engine failure and inlet debris strike
ders: fan blade inspections were accelerated with ultrasound checks
yanilgi: The engine didn't explode from fire. One fan blade snapped from fatigue, and the debris hit the fuselage.
tartisma: A similar blade failure happened two years earlier. Should inspections tighten after the first one?
basliklar: Why Southwest Flight 1380's Engine Failed
The Fatigue Crack in One Fan Blade
soru: Inspect after the first, or the second?
sahneler: At cruising altitude, a jet's engine suddenly blew apart.
Debris shattered a window, and one passenger was killed.
The cause was a single fan blade.
A fatigue crack had grown inside it.
When it snapped, the engine's inlet broke up.
Fragments struck the fuselage and the window gave way.
The captain still landed the jet safely in Philadelphia.
Fan blades were then checked more often with ultrasound.

baslik: Two Jumbo Jets, One Runway, and a Misunderstood Word
sonuc: saw two jumbo jets collide on a foggy runway
tetik: a take-off started without clearance in fog
mekanizma: ambiguous radio phrasing, blocked transmissions and zero visibility on a single runway
ders: standard radio phrases were enforced and the word take-off reserved for clearance
zincir: TAKE-OFF WITH A JET ON THE RUNWAY
yanilgi: No machine failed. The disaster was built from words: an ambiguous phrase and two radio calls that cancelled each other out.
tartisma: The captain was the airline's most senior pilot. How do you question someone that senior?
basliklar: Why the Tenerife Disaster Happened
The Radio Call Nobody Heard
sahneler: Two jumbo jets collided on a runway in Tenerife.
It was the deadliest accident in aviation history: five hundred eighty three people died.
Fog hid the runway, and one jet was still taxiing on it.
The other began its take-off without clearance.
A vague radio phrase sounded like permission.
Two calls overlapped, and the warning was lost in noise.
No machine failed that day.
Aviation radio phrases were standardized afterward.

baslik: The Wrong Bolts Let a Windscreen Blow Out
sonuc: lost a windscreen in flight, pulling the captain out
tetik: a windscreen fitted with bolts that were too small
mekanizma: undersized bolts unable to hold the windscreen against cabin pressure
ders: maintenance procedures and parts identification were tightened
yanilgi: The windscreen itself didn't break. It was held in by bolts slightly too small to grip.
tartisma: The engineer picked bolts by matching them by eye at night. How much should a critical job depend on one person?
basliklar: Why British Airways Flight 5390 Lost Its Windscreen
The Bolts That Were Slightly Too Small
soru: Match by eye, or check the part number?
sahneler: At seventeen thousand feet, a cockpit windscreen blew out.
Suddenly, the captain was sucked halfway out of the aircraft.
The crew held on to his legs while the co-pilot landed.
He survived.
The windscreen had been replaced the night before.
Most of the bolts used were slightly too small.
They couldn't hold against the cabin pressure.
Maintenance checks on critical parts were tightened afterward.

baslik: A Misaligned Oil Pipe Blew Apart an A380 Engine
tetik: a fatigue crack in an oil pipe made with a thin wall
mekanizma: misaligned counterbore thinning an oil feed stub pipe, leading to fatigue, oil fire and turbine disc failure
ders: engines with the faulty pipe were inspected and replaced
yanilgi: The engine didn't fail from bird strike or fuel. A manufacturing error left one oil pipe's wall too thin.
tartisma: Nobody died, but debris cut wiring and a fuel tank. Would you call that a near-miss or a disaster averted by luck?
basliklar: Why Qantas Flight 32's Engine Exploded
The Thin-Walled Pipe That Burst an A380 Engine
sahneler: Minutes after leaving Singapore, an A380's engine exploded.
In seconds, debris tore through the wing and cut wiring.
The crew spent nearly two hours working through failures, then landed safely.
The cause was a small oil pipe inside the engine.
It had been machined off-centre, leaving its wall too thin.
A fatigue crack leaked oil, which caught fire.
A turbine disc overheated and burst.
Engines with the faulty pipe were inspected and replaced.

baslik: The Stall Warning Pilots Pulled Against
sonuc: stalled and crashed into a house near Buffalo
tetik: a pilot pulling back when the stall warning shook the controls
mekanizma: inappropriate response to the stick shaker, deepening an aerodynamic stall
ders: US pilot training, rest and experience rules were overhauled
yanilgi: Ice wasn't the main cause. The stall followed the crew's reaction to the warning, not a loss of lift from icing.
tartisma: Both pilots were tired after long commutes. How much of safety depends on sleep?
basliklar: Why Colgan Air Flight 3407 Crashed
The Warning That Said Push, Not Pull
soru: Would you push the nose down?
sahneler: Near Buffalo, a commuter plane suddenly stalled and fell onto a house.
Everyone aboard was killed, along with one person on the ground.
As the plane slowed, its stall warning shook the controls.
The right response was to push the nose down.
The captain pulled back instead.
That deepened the stall until recovery was impossible.
Both pilots had been tired.
US rules on pilot training and rest were then overhauled.
